lines.text: The first English and French colonies in the Caribbean, sugar fields and fortresses, and the smallest country in the Americas. This is Saint Kitts and Nevis.
English settlers arrived in 1623, and the French soon after. In 1626 they joined to massacre the Kalinago, the island's first people.
The French founded Basseterre on Saint Kitts, the town that would become the capital.
Sugar, grown by enslaved Africans, made the islands rich, and the British built a mighty fortress on Brimstone Hill to guard them.
On Nevis, Alexander Hamilton was born. He would help found the United States and become its first Treasury Secretary.
Robert Bradshaw was born, a labour leader who would become the islands' first premier.
Kennedy Simmonds was born, the future first prime minister of the independent nation.
Kim Collins was born, the sprinter who would become world champion over a hundred metres in 2003.
The same year saw the birth of Terrance Drew, who became prime minister in 2022.
In 1983 Saint Kitts and Nevis became independent from Britain, the smallest country in the Americas.
Small in size but long in history, these two islands keep their own proud story.
